denial.expiry_check: python tools/gdl/probe.py game/anim/atree AtreeMatch --revert-best after editing both inside AtreeMatch and at file scope; the refusal must lead and $LASTEXITCODE must be 5.
denial.falsifier: A partial function-scoped restore that prints no refusal block at all, or one that exits 0.
denial.premise_measurement: Reproduced on game/anim/atree::AtreeMatch in both partial shapes. Helper-lift (a static helper hoisted to file scope): probe printed THREE loud blocks -- REVERT LEFT A COUPLED FILE-SCOPE HALF naming the added fndef, REVERT IS PARTIAL naming src/game/anim/atree.c (+5/-0 vs HEAD), and REFUSED TO BANK. Sibling-body edit: two blocks, no coupled warning (correctly -- no file-scope item moved). run-45 item 6 had already closed the silent half. What survived is that BOTH exited 0, and that the headline read `READOUT   real 0 (insns T44/O44, multiset 0t)` -- the same shape, column and width as `BASELINE  real 0 (insns T44/O44, multiset 0t)` -- printed ABOVE the refusal. Those are the two things a script and a reader go by, and they are what the fix changes: exit 5, refusal first, number relabelled NOT A VERDICT.
denial.scope: Item 3's stated symptom -- that a partial --revert-best is SILENT -- on probe.py as of 65348245e. Not a denial of the item's direction.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: For any of the 11, if the ordered datum sequences are identical then no transposition exists and CANDIDATE is the whole story; run it over all 11 in one pass with fndiff.datum_relocs.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- the ordered-sequence comparison was not run; the calibration measured the multiset verdict and the row-set permutation only, and those two agree that these 11 are not wrong CONSTANTS. Whether they are wrong ORDERS is unmeasured.
hypothesis.statement: The 11 CANDIDATE rows item 4 demoted are not all artifacts: a positional row whose function reads VALUE-EQUAL can still be a genuine TRANSPOSITION spread across non-adjacent offsets, which the row-set permutation test misses because the differing labels pair up elsewhere in the function. Re-screen those 11 by comparing each function's ORDERED datum sequence (not its multiset) against the target's, which is the one comparison neither the multiset nor the row-set permutation makes.
